Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma ( PDAC ) is one of the most lethal malignancies. To improve its outcome, reliable biomarkers are urgently needed. In this study, we aimed to elucidate the key molecules involved in PDAC progression using proteomics approaches. First, we undertook 2‐D electrophoresis to identify the proteins overexpressed in PDAC tissues. Following the analysis of agarose gel spots, cofilin‐1 was identified and verified as a candidate protein commonly upregulated in PDAC tissues. In immunohistochemistry, cofilin‐1 was strongly expressed in the cytoplasm of PDAC cells. Samples were divided into two groups based on the level of cofilin‐1 expression. The high expression group showed significantly higher incidence of hematogenous dissemination in relapsed patients than the low expression group ( P = 0.0083). In in vitro experiments, knockdown of cofilin‐1 significantly decreased chemotaxis in PDAC cell lines. After we confirmed that cofilin‐1 was secreted from PDAC cells, we established a detection system for the immune‐complex of cofilin‐1 in sera. Using this system, we measured the IC levels of cofilin‐1 in sera and observed that the IC levels of cofilin‐1 in PDAC patients were higher than those in healthy volunteers and patients with pancreatitis ( PDAC vs . healthy volunteers, P < 0.0001; PDAC vs . patients with pancreatitis, P < 0.026). Notably, the IC levels of cofilin‐1 showed a stepwise increase during PDAC progression ( P = 0.0034), and high IC levels of cofilin‐1 indicated poor prognosis of patients after surgery ( P = 0.039). These results suggest that the IC of cofilin‐1 in sera is a potentially attractive serum biomarker for the prognosis of PDAC . Abbreviations 2‐DE two‐dimensional gel electrophoresis BAG3 BCL2‐associated athanogene 3 CA19‐9 Cancer antigen 19‐9 HV healthy volunteer IC immune‐complex IHC immunohistochemistry MS mass spectrometry PDAC pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma PD‐ECGF platelet‐derived endothelial cell growth factor PT pancreatitis ROC receiver operating characteristic SSH slingshot Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is one of the most lethal malignancies among various solid tumors with an extremely low 5‐year survival rate of 7%. 1 Advances in the field of clinical biomarker discovery are developing to not only provide useful tools for patient stratification, but also to offer potential therapeutic targets and revealing molecular mechanistic insights behind disease progression, thereby facilitating exploitation of novel therapies. However, identifying a desired biomarker still faces significant challenges. 2 In line with this, some attractive biomarkers for PDAC have been discovered and tested in a clinical setting as diagnostic and prognostic indicators. Despite the identification of candidate proteins or peptides that have potentially been useful and reliable in translational research, there are still some critical limitations for clinical application. Of the various possible human samples, serum or plasma samples are reasonable to use as they contain the richest and most detailed source of information (e.g. DNA, RNA, proteins, and peptides) about the physiological state of the body as well as being less invasive to collect. Thus, blood samples would potentially have a pivotal role in ascertaining the status of cancer progression in patients. Emerging new technology for serum proteomics using mass spectrometry, such as surface‐enhanced laser desorption/ionization–time of flight or matrix‐assisted laser desorption/ionization–time of flight, enables the identification of protein profiles composed of isolated or clustered peaks that differ according to molecular weight. 3 Although these techniques have some advantages for detecting differences in protein profiling, including post‐translational modifications, it is still difficult to apply in clinical scenarios due to the complexity of optimization for standard use. Antibody‐based proteomic approaches such as the standard ELISA method or the measurement of autoimmune antibodies are primarily carried out in the examination of target protein or peptide levels in blood samples. 4 Focusing on these targets in sera, the IC has recently been highlighted as a novel biomarker in blood samples of cancer patients. 5 , 6 , 7 , 8 Recently, it has been reported that a high‐throughput screening method for native autoantigen–autoantibody complexes using antibody microarrays provides serum biomarkers as a useful tool for disease detection and characterization. 9 In this study, we initially used a gel‐based proteomic approach, 2‐DE, to analyze the comprehensive protein profile and identify biomarkers for PDAC. Subsequently, we have attempted to establish a detection system for candidate proteins involved with PDAC progression by measuring the serum levels of patients. Finally, we revealed that the IC level in sera is associated with cancer progression and may potentially provide a useful prognostic serum biomarker for PDAC.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study comprehensively investigated cofilin-1 as a biomarker for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). It identified cofilin-1 overexpression in PDAC tissues and its secretion from PDAC cells, confirming its association with hematogenous metastasis and finding that its knockdown reduces cancer cell chemotaxis. Furthermore, serum immune-complex (IC) levels of cofilin-1 were validated as a diagnostic marker, differentiating PDAC patients from controls, correlating with disease progression, and serving as a prognostic indicator for poor patient outcomes after surgery.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Biomarker discovery, identification, and validation for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) diagnosis and prognosis, including siRNA-mediated gene knockdown in cell lines.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study focused on identifying and validating endogenous biomarker levels in PDAC patients, healthy volunteers, and pancreatitis patients. Experimental interventions included siRNA knockdown of cofilin-1 at 1, 5, and 10 nM concentrations in PDAC cell lines. Tumor tissue overexpression of cofilin-1 was defined as a 2-fold increase, and immunohistochemistry categorized patients into weak (25.4%) and strong (74.6%) expression groups; no therapeutic dose comparisons were reported.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) tissues, normal pancreas tissues, invasive cancer cells, and cultured PDAC cell lines (PANC-1, Capan-1) and their culture medium.
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein Level (expression via 2-DE, LC-MS/MS, Western blotting, IHC), Protein Secretion, Protein Function (via gene knockdown).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Identified with a 2-fold increase in PDAC tumor tissues versus normal; markedly overexpressed in 9 out of 9 tumor tissue samples; strongly expressed in the cytoplasm of PDAC cells, with positive expression in 96.6% (57/59) of invasive cancer cells. The strong expression group showed significantly higher incidence of hematogenous dissemination (P = 0.0083) and liver/lung metastases (P = 0.0083) in relapsed patients, with 100% of stage IV patients belonging to this group. Cofilin-1 protein with a 21-kDa band was also observed to increase in cultured cell medium, indicating secretion. Knockdown of cofilin-1 significantly decreased chemotaxis in PDAC cell lines in a concentration-dependent manner.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An actin depolymerizing factor involved in actin filament remodeling, essential for cell motility, chemotaxis, and invasion of tumor cells, thereby mediating cancer progression and hematogenous dissemination.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) pathogenesis, tumor progression, distant metastasis, post-surgical recurrence, and in vitro pancreatic cancer cell motility/invasion and secretion.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A candidate biomarker for PDAC, strongly associated with advanced cancer progression, increased risk of hematogenous dissemination and liver/lung metastases, and functionally involved in tumor cell motility and invasion.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Serum IC levels were significantly higher in PDAC patients compared to healthy volunteers (P < 0.0001) and patients with pancreatitis (P < 0.026). These levels showed a stepwise increase correlated with UICC stage during PDAC progression (P = 0.0034). High IC levels indicated poor prognosis after surgery (P = 0.039) and were significantly correlated with overall survival on univariate analysis (P = 0.042). The combination of cofilin-1 IC and CA19-9 had an AUC of 0.900, improving upon CA19-9 alone (0.866) for distinguishing cancer.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A potential diagnostic and prognostic serum biomarker for PDAC, differentiating patients from controls, correlating with disease stage, and predicting poor patient outcomes after surgery and overall survival.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Area under the ROC curve (AUC) value of 0.866 for distinguishing cancer from non-cancer patients. Improved diagnostic performance when combined with cofilin-1 IC (AUC 0.900).
